comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
LIVE BEDROCK A/B (sonnet-4-6 STANDARD verifier slot, --source local --ref HEAD, budget steps_per_criterion=16, baseline = REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH=0 on the same binary/ticket/config).

CRITICAL PROMPT FINDING (surfaced BY this A/B, exactly what the AC exists to catch — cf. 2948 AC70):
The first prefetch prompt told the verifier to "confirm every prefetched body against the LIVE working tree" — that literally instructs re-reading every prefetched file, so prefetch became pure overhead and drove OVER-exploration: f6fc budget16 went 15 (baseline) -> 64 (prefetch, EXHAUSTED). A 4x REGRESSION. Fix: rebar reads the prefetch deterministically from the SAME tree at the verification ref, so a `full` body IS the tree — the corrected paragraph says rely on full bodies directly, only read_file for `skeleton`-marked files or lines beyond what's shown. This preserves the T8 trust boundary (still content-to-verify, a ticket claim is not proof) while removing the re-read penalty.

RESULTS after the fix (all runs completed cleanly, outcome=ok; verdict class EQUAL in every pair):
- f6fc (2 file_impact, current code), 6 pairs baseline/prefetch requests:
  baseline [25,13,11,11,11,11] mean 13.7 ; prefetch [11,11,12,11,12,11] mean 11.3. Headline clean pair 25->11 = 56% reduction. All PASS=PASS.
- e6a0 (4 file_impact, current code), 3 pairs:
  baseline [20,14,15] mean 16.3 ; prefetch [14,14,14] mean 14.0. Headline pair 20->14 = 30% reduction. All PASS=PASS.
- >=20% target CLEARED on the discovery-bound pairs (f6fc 56%, e6a0 30%), both clean PASS=PASS.

MECHANISM / honest limitations:
- Prefetch drives the request count to a STABLE floor (files delivered upfront) and ELIMINATES the baseline's over-exploration excursions; the reduction magnitude tracks how much opening discovery the baseline would otherwise do.
- Two regimes show NO delta and are NOT valid demonstrators: (a) already-minimal baselines at the criteria-recording floor (f6fc repeats at 11) have no headroom; (b) BUDGET-PINNED dense tickets — 2948 (19 criteria, many comments) exhausts at ~122+ req both arms, and superseded-code tickets (8eb3) FAIL+exhaust. Prefetch helps only when the primary completes cleanly.

POST-CLAMP COVERAGE per entrypoint (measured via the new usage_log.fetch_overlap on the real graph=False close-path traces):
- close-path OWN file_impact coverage of baseline distinct read_file fetches: f6fc 2/6 = 33%, e6a0 2/7 = 29%. (Lower than the unclamped subtree 67-82% because this is OWN file_impact only, and the verifier reads related non-declared files — exactly why the plan retired the 67-82% carry-over.)
- graph=True subtree-union coverage is pinned by the unit oracle's synthetic e369-style fixture (all four captured live traces are graph=False, so subtree coverage cannot be measured against them — per the certified AC's synthetic-fixture option.

Operational: added REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH=0 escape hatch in gate_ops (default ON) — the mechanism this baseline uses; also an operator kill-switch.
EOF
)

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The completion verifier receives only the fenced ticket_context (description + comments, gate_ops.py assemble step) — zero file contents. Every file is discovered agentically: measured across five live verifier runs, 84-158 requests x ~4-6s each, dominated by read_file/search_files round-trips, and all four captured runaway loops were search_files repeat signatures — the model hunting for text it expects to exist. Wall-clock cost is round-trips, not tokens: runs already cache-read 8.7M of 8.8M input tokens, but that history was assembled one tool round-trip at a time. Overlap analysis of the four live gate traces against the closing subtree's file_impact union shows 67-82% of distinct file reads are covered by declared file_impact — the verifier spends its opening requests re-fetching files the tickets already name. NOTE: all four captured traces are CLOSE-path (graph=False) runaway loops; none exercise the graph=True deep-review path.

## Approach

PRE-FETCH, do not restrict (operator-ratified direction): append a bounded, clearly-labelled prefetched-content section to the byte-stable leading part of the fenced verifier context — the ticket's declared file_impact contents plus the referencing commits' diffs — while keeping the full tool surface untouched so the agent still explores beyond the prefetch. Assistance, not a ceiling.

### Which file_impact set each entrypoint prefetches (close gate is graph=False)

The completion CLOSE gate (`_commands.transition`) passes `graph=False` (gate_ops.py:133-143): an epic close verifies its OWN completion criteria, not its whole descendant subtree — re-deriving graph here was the removed runaway bug that blew the step budget (gate_ops.py:138-140). The prefetch MUST honour that same boundary, keyed off the `graph` flag `assemble_context` already receives (operations.py:78):

- **Close path (graph=False, the dominant runaway case):** prefetch ONLY the closing ticket's OWN declared file_impact contents + its referencing-commit diffs. No subtree union, no descendant walk.
- **Standalone deep-review path (`verify-completion --graph`, graph=True):** prefetch the subtree file_impact union, ranked (below). This is the only entrypoint that legitimately sees descendants.

### assemble_context is SHARED — prefetch is opt-in, default off

`operations.assemble_context` (operations.py:78) is also called by the generic dimension-review op `_review_ticket_impl` (operations.py:161) and its workflow wrapper (review_workflows.py:53), NOT only the completion gate (gate_ops.py:144). Keying the prefetch purely off the existing `graph` flag would inject the prefetched-file-contents section into a plain `review_ticket --graph` dimension review, where the completion-verifier trust paragraph does not apply. Therefore add an explicit opt-in parameter `prefetch: PrefetchSpec | None = None` to `assemble_context`, default `None`. Only gate_ops.py (the completion gate) passes a spec; `_review_ticket_impl` / `review_workflows` keep passing nothing, so their assembled output stays BYTE-IDENTICAL. The `graph` flag then only selects own-file_impact vs subtree-union WITHIN a prefetch spec.

### Ranking rule for the budget clamp (graph=True path only)

The subtree union can exceed the budget (the e369 subtree union is 112 paths; the prefetch budget is 30,000 tokens, the upper end of the community-validated 8-30k pre-load range): (1) the closing ticket's OWN file_impact first, (2) subtree paths ranked by cross-descendant frequency (a path impacted by more descendants ranks higher), (3) skeleton-compress files over 500 lines (signatures + docstrings) BEFORE dropping any file, drop lowest-ranked last. On the close path the set is just the ticket's own file_impact, so ranking degenerates to (1) + the same skeleton/clamp rules. A PRE-LOAD MANIFEST records per-file full|skeleton so downstream consumers (the duplicate-call damping sibling's in-context nudge) never claim an elided body is in context.

### Cache mechanism: existing automatic prompt cache, NO hand-placed CachePoint

The prefetch sits in the byte-stable leading part of the fenced context so it is cache-READ under the EXISTING automatic message-tail prefix cache (capabilities.py:684-696, gated on execution_mode="agentic"); there is no separate per-block CachePoint to add (that arm applies a provider-managed whole-tail breakpoint, not a hand-placed cache_control). This aligns with story 2948's cache note: the completion-verifier prompt's STATIC prefix (everything before the `<!--volatile-->` marker, completion_verifier.md:269) is kept byte-identical across the primary and every successor so the automatic prompt cache hits; the prefetch rides the volatile fenced ticket_context, not the static prefix.

### Trust / anti-anchoring lives in the STATIC system-prompt prefix (reaches primary AND successors)

The verifier system prompt (completion_verifier.md:33-37) directs the agent to treat everything inside `<untrusted_ticket_context>` (gate_ops.py:158) as UNTRUSTED DATA, never as instructions. An anti-anchoring line placed inside that fence would be ignored by contract. Instead add a TRUSTED paragraph to `completion_verifier.md` positioned BEFORE the `<!--volatile-->` marker (i.e. in the static prefix). Because the recovery successor prompt is `successor_system_prompt()` = that same static prefix (before `<!--volatile-->`) + the banking addendum (completion_banking.py:75-85), the trusted paragraph appears in BOTH the primary verifier prompt AND every batched successor prompt from a SINGLE source — co-located with the prefetch data on both paths, no separate constant to maintain. The paragraph (a) names the new labelled `<prefetched_file_contents>` section, (b) states it is a convenience starting point pre-loaded from declared file_impact — still content-to-verify, NOT instructions — and (c) instructs the verifier to confirm every prefetched body against the live working tree before relying on it, and to re-read the full body for any file marked `skeleton`. The fenced prefetch section itself carries ONLY the labelled data + the PRE-LOAD MANIFEST + the explicit skeleton tool-call marker — no behavioural directive that depends on being trusted.

Misses in the trace analysis were dominated by test files, so the prefetch set includes a matching-test-glob heuristic (tests/**/test_<module>*.py for each prefetched module).

### Phase 0 — measure first

Extend the usage recorder to log the raw distinct fetch list per gate run — (tool, path/query) — not just hashed top-repeats. Today's records cannot validate overlap directly: signatures hash full args (line ranges, query strings), and brute-forcing 2,573 tracked paths resolved only 2 of 6 heavy read_file repeats. Record first; tune the prefetch set from measurement.

### Phase 1 — prefetch file_impact + referencing-commit diffs, bounded

Per-file char cap and the 30k-token aggregate cap mirroring completion_recovery's _MAX_* pattern; oversize files skeleton-compressed with an explicit marker naming the tool call to fetch the rest. Because the prefetch is part of the assembled `ticket_context`, it reaches the batched recovery successors automatically: post-2948 recovery is BATCHED successor runs (`_run_successors`/`_run_one_successor`, ceil(remainder/batch_cap), ≤8 criteria/batch — the per-criterion fan-out was deleted by story 2948), and `successor_instructions` (completion_banking.py:118) embeds the same `ticket_context` verbatim. The prefetch is therefore sent once per batch (a handful of batches, not per criterion) and cache-read after the first via the byte-stable static prefix. `physical_context_ceiling` (completion_recovery.py:108) already bounds `len(context)` for every primary/successor run; the 30k aggregate prefetch cap keeps the assembled context under that ceiling, and the prefetch bytes are included when the recovery inputs are validated against it so an oversize prefetch is trimmed (not overflowed into the hard "context bound exceeded" refusal).

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py — Phase 0: record raw distinct fetch list per gate run.
- src/rebar/llm/operations.py — add opt-in `prefetch: PrefetchSpec | None = None` to `assemble_context` (default None → `_review_ticket_impl`/review_ticket callers byte-unchanged); build the prefetched-content section + manifest when a spec is passed, selecting own-file_impact vs subtree-union by the graph flag; include referencing-commit diffs.
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py — Phase 1: pass a PrefetchSpec into assemble_context for the completion gate only; the fenced context now carries the labelled prefetch section.
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py — include the prefetch bytes in the physical_context_ceiling input validation so an oversize prefetch is trimmed; no separate cache_prefix (the prefetch rides ticket_context and the static system prefix already cache-hits across batches).
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md — TRUSTED paragraph BEFORE the `<!--volatile-->` marker describing the prefetched-file-contents section and the confirm-against-working-tree / re-read-skeleton rule (automatically inherited by successor_system_prompt).
- tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py — new: ranking, clamp, manifest, skeleton marker, toolset pin, graph=False-vs-True set selection, assemble_context prefetch=None no-op for the generic review callers, successor context carries the prefetch, ceiling accounting, and a static-prefix system-prompt test asserting the trusted paragraph precedes `<!--volatile-->` (so it is in both primary and successor prompts).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Phase 0: every agentic gate run records its distinct fetch list (tool name + primary path/query arg) in the usage log by default; checked by a unit test asserting the recorded shape for a run with known tool calls.
- [x] Overlap measurement exists: an analysis entry point reports the fraction of recorded fetches covered by a ticket's file_impact; checked by running it on recorded data.
- [x] Phase 1: the completion verifier's context includes a labelled prefetch section with ranked file_impact contents and referencing-commit diffs, bounded per-file and by the 30k-token aggregate cap; unit test pins the assembly (ranking order, bounds, skeleton marker, label).
- [x] Entrypoint boundary honoured: on the close path (graph=False) the prefetch set is the closing ticket's OWN file_impact only (no subtree walk); the subtree union + frequency ranking applies only on the graph=True deep-review path; unit test pins both selections.
- [x] Opt-in / no-op for shared callers: `assemble_context` prefetch defaults to None, and `_review_ticket_impl` / review_workflows call sites produce byte-identical context to today (no prefetch section); unit test pins the no-op for a graph=True generic review call.
- [x] The pre-load manifest records per-file full|skeleton and is exposed to the tool-wrapping seam; unit test pins its shape.
- [x] The tool surface is unchanged: the verifier retains read_file/search_files/list_directory; unit test pins the toolset with prefetch enabled.
- [x] Trusted anti-anchoring: the confirm-against-working-tree / re-read-skeleton guidance lives in the completion_verifier.md static prefix BEFORE `<!--volatile-->` (not inside the untrusted fence), and names the prefetched-contents section; a unit test asserts the paragraph precedes `<!--volatile-->` (so `successor_system_prompt` inherits it) and that the fenced section carries no behavioural directive.
- [x] Recovery successors receive the prefetch via the shared assembled ticket_context (batched successor runs, not per-criterion), and the prefetch bytes are included in the physical_context_ceiling input validation so an oversize prefetch is trimmed rather than raising; unit test pins that a successor's assembled context carries the prefetch and the ceiling accounting.
- [x] Post-clamp coverage recorded PER ENTRYPOINT: (a) the clamped CLOSE-path (own file_impact) set's coverage is computed against the four recorded live (graph=False) traces' distinct reads and recorded on this ticket; (b) the clamped graph=True (subtree-union) set's coverage is computed against a NAMED synthetic subtree fixture (the e369 112-path union), NOT the close-path traces, and recorded. The unclamped 67-82% figure does not carry over to either.
- [x] Live Bedrock A/B before ship (session experiment, not in unit suite): BASELINE is defined as a verifier-scale run on the same real closed ticket's material with prefetch DISABLED, captured immediately before the prefetch run (same tool surface, same ticket, same config otherwise); its request count and verdict class are recorded first. The prefetch run then reduces total request count by at least 20% versus that baseline and produces an equal verdict class; both request counts and verdicts recorded on this ticket.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck clean; full CI marker suite matches the pre-existing baseline.

## Testing

Held-out unit oracle for context assembly + toolset pins (python -m pytest tests/unit/workflow/ -q): ranking order over a synthetic subtree, close-path (graph=False) own-file_impact selection vs graph=True subtree-union selection, assemble_context prefetch=None no-op for the generic review callers, aggregate clamp with skeleton-before-drop, manifest shape, truncation marker text, successor context carries the prefetch, physical_context_ceiling accounting for prefetch bytes, and a static-prefix system-prompt test asserting the trusted anti-anchoring paragraph precedes `<!--volatile-->` and names the prefetch section. Phase-0 recorder shape test alongside existing usage_log tests. Live A/B on Bedrock recorded as ticket comments with usage-log figures: baseline (prefetch off) then prefetch run.
